findings.claim: A small local variance bound or finite uncertainty number cannot alone establish low error probability at acquisition: single-tone ML/block estimators have a threshold region where errors can depart sharply from the local CRB.
findings.support_locator: S1 abstract describes threshold analysis for one ML algorithm; S4 abstract relates threshold onset to Barankin-vs-CRB divergence.
findings.decision_implication: For the proposed <=0.10 Hz / >=95% target, record absolute error, gross-error/outlier rate, and acquisition/nonpublication outcomes by SNR and dwell; do not validate solely against estimator-reported variance or a CRB.
findings.assumptions: The referenced single-tone models are useful approximations for isolated pilot windows.
findings.applicability_gap: Noise, amplitude envelope, modulation/auxiliary activity, estimator, and signal-present decision differ from the hypothetical receiver task; no target feasibility result follows.
findings.next_discriminator: At each hypothetical reference level, compare empirical error tails and detection outcomes across a short dwell sweep (including the 6 s endpoint), with absent-tone controls and offsets both near and away from search edges.

findings.claim: A computationally light single-tone frequency estimator can be competitive with ML at moderately high SNR, while performance depends on model and SNR; there is a meaningful practical baseline to compare against before adding a more elaborate tracker.
findings.support_locator: S2 institutional abstract lines 27-29; S1 abstract documents finite-sample ML/DFT algorithms and threshold effects.
findings.decision_implication: Retain a straightforward block periodogram/DFT-based acquisition plus sub-bin refinement as a comparator against phase-difference or tracking approaches. Count compute and latency alongside accuracy.
findings.assumptions: The tone is reasonably stationary over each block and the search captures its main lobe.
findings.applicability_gap: Kay’s summarized result is for a complex sinusoid in complex white Gaussian noise; it does not establish performance for a real sampled tone with ramps, payload activity, or this implementation.
findings.next_discriminator: Run a matched capture comparison of block spectral refinement and a phase-difference estimator using identical sample apertures and search bands; report tail errors, false admissions, and work per update.

findings.claim: Differential-phase estimators expose a tradeoff in delay: larger phase separation can reduce high-SNR variance in some regimes, but estimator range, low-SNR behavior, and complexity also change.
findings.support_locator: IEEE abstract/metadata for 2006 paper, DOI 10.1109/TCOMM.2006.869864; publisher page could not be opened.
findings.decision_implication: If phase continuity is trustworthy, a small delay sweep is a useful candidate discriminator; it should be compared both with independent-aperture frequency estimates and with injected phase discontinuities/retunes.
findings.assumptions: Complex phase observations are available and phase evolves continuously over the selected delay.
findings.applicability_gap: Paper model is a single complex sinusoid in AWGN; supplied code excerpt distinguishes explicit retunes and phase continuity, and native chunking may not preserve phase across capture resets.
findings.next_discriminator: Measure empirical frequency error versus phase-difference lag and SNR; separately test arbitrary 137/4096 chunk partitions of the same uninterrupted samples and announced resets.

findings.claim: Frequency drift or multiplicative phase/frequency variation broadens a tone and degrades estimators derived for stationary sinusoids; coherent and noncoherent signal-to-noise conditions both matter.
findings.support_locator: Strathprints abstract lines 17-20; peer-reviewed IEEE article metadata at lines 14-16.
findings.decision_implication: Separate stationary pure-tone estimator comparisons from representative auxiliary/payload and time-varying captures; do not infer that accumulating a longer aperture always improves practical error under changing frequency or amplitude.
findings.assumptions: The cited Doppler-spread model is conceptually relevant to drift or time-varying phase, not necessarily identical to the receiver’s variation.
findings.applicability_gap: The article’s multiplicative-noise/spread model and covariance-angle algorithms may not match this receiver’s oscillator drift or signal envelope.
findings.next_discriminator: With identical mean offsets and SNR, compare clean stationary captures to captures with controlled frequency drift/phase-noise or amplitude interruptions, plotting error against aperture and whether phase is retained.

unresolved: Whether the target precision and 6-second deadline are attainable for the actual signal, sample rate, front-end, and presence definition; this requires matched measurements or simulation in the authorized engineering assignment.
Whether continuity across delivered chunks is preserved in the actual capture path; supplied source excerpt alone does not establish runtime behavior.
Exact thresholds and confidence calibration for the specific estimator under real noise, auxiliary activity, ramps, and frequency drift.
stop_reason: Sufficient decision-useful evidence gathered within 13 of 16 logical operations (6 searches, 7 opens including 3 failed opens); additional source hunting would add less value than the concrete matched discriminators. Finished within the 12-minute target.
escalation_ready: Yes. For Sol/Astra: retain stationary single-tone block refinement as a matched baseline; prioritize empirical error-tail/false-admission tests over CRB or reported-uncertainty claims; compare phase-delay/continuous tracking only with explicit continuity/reset controls; include drift/amplitude-mismatch cases and verify chunk-partition invariance. No algorithm, feasibility, or architecture selected.
